'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Communal conflicts in Nigeria]]
**Gunmen launch simultaneous attacks on three communities in [[Niger State]], [[Nigeria]], killing at least 46 people and [[Kidnapping in Nigeria|kidnapping]] a number of others. [https://www.thedailystar.net/news/world/news/46-killed-fresh-nigeria-attacks-4106461 (AFP via ''The Daily Star'')]
*[[Islamist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**Seven [[Ghanaians|Ghanaian]] traders are killed when [[Ansarul Islam (Sahel)|Islamist insurgent]]s attack [[Titao]], [[Loroum Province]], [[Burkina Faso]], with the assailants burning the bodies and a vehicle. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/seven-ghanaian-traders-killed-burkina-faso-by-suspected-islamists-ghana-says-2026-02-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Gunmen attack a bar in [[Puebla (city)|Puebla]], [[Mexico]], killing three people and wounding five others. Authorities confirm the arrest of four criminals related to the attack. [https://aristeguinoticias.com/1402/mexico/ataque-armado-en-bar-sala-de-despecho-de-puebla-deja-tres-muertos/ (Aristegui Noticias)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Ukraine and the International Monetary Fund]]
**[[Ukraine]] and the [[International Monetary Fund]] agree to modify conditions for a proposed [[US$]]8.2 billion, four-year lending program, easing certain requirements including planned [[Taxation in Ukraine|tax]] increases on entrepreneurs above a higher revenue threshold. [https://www.reuters.com/business/ukraine-imf-ease-conditions-new-82-billion-loan-program-2026-02-14/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Ethiopia–Sudan relations]]
**[[Ethiopia]] revokes [[Reuters]] journalists' accreditation in response to an article on February 10 that alleged the [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|Ethiopian military]] was supporting the [[Rapid Support Forces]] in the [[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]] by running secret [[Training camp|training camps]] for its fighters. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-13/ethiopia-revokes-reuters-journalists-accreditation-after-expose (Bloomberg)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Death and funeral of Alexei Navalny]]
**[[France]], [[Germany]], the [[Netherlands]], [[Sweden]], and the [[United Kingdom]] assess that [[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|Russian opposition leader]] [[Alexei Navalny]] died in prison after being poisoned by [[epibatidine]], a neurotoxin found in South American [[poison dart frog]]s. [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/russia/russian-opposition-leader-alexei-navalny-poisoned-deadly-dart-frog-rcna259064 (NBC News)]
